reviewer: Codex independent source review; not author of Grok exporter
verdict: APPROVE frozen9516e84e reader/decoder source for root-owned build and exact-wrapper integration. No concrete byte/length/digest/metadata-policy success blocker found under the specified snapshot/CR-normalization policy. This is not a source-independent runtime outcome, producer-closed proof, supervisor/ID-layout approval or desktop qualification.

verified_findings.subject: Typed exact CLI before file access
verified_findings.finding: argc/option order, absolute non-root directory argument without dot/parent segments, lowercase48hex nonce, exact session|application kind and live|closed phase are checked before open. Kind selects only its fixed two-entry table. No directory scan, arbitrary record-name argument, spawn, device/registry operation or environment-based fallback exists in the explicit reader call graph. O_NOFOLLOW protects the final directory and record components; ancestor symlink exclusion is not claimed.

verified_findings.subject: Fixed required record sets and caps
verified_findings.finding: Session captures only session-result.txt<=16384 and manager-status.log<=65536. Application captures only stdout/stderr log files<=8192 each. Before-read size is checked before allocation/read; all two files are required in both phases. Extra directory files are ignored, never scanned/exported. Missing/refused/read-failed files leave a failing exporter result; missing/refused lines or incomplete required sets cannot decode successfully.

verified_findings.subject: Private owned anchored read-only descriptors
verified_findings.finding: Directory open is O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, with actual fstat directory type, euid and exact0700. Each fixed openat uses O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK; fstat requires regular file, nlink1, current euid, exact0600 including special permission bits and bounded nonnegative size. There are no file writes, truncations, creations, chmods or unlinks. FIFO open is nonblocking and type refusal precedes read. Metadata checks are snapshots of the held object, not a persistent ownership lease or ACL audit.

verified_findings.subject: Actual read size and phase semantics
verified_findings.finding: Read consumes exactly the accepted initial size with partial-read/EINTR handling; short EOF/error refuses. Post-read fstat requires same device/inode and non-shrinkage; closed also requires equal observed size. Live may report later growth while retaining the captured bounded prefix. SHA binds the actual buffered bytes. No read beyond the initial accepted size occurs. These observations do not prove atomic contents against a hostile same-size overwrite or that the writer has exited; root's producer/phase ownership must establish the intended append-only/live or retired/closed conditions.

verified_findings.subject: Checked success finalization and SHA/index/count wire
verified_findings.finding: Success path closes each file before hashing/emitting its complete record and checks close result. Main checks directory close and final fflush/ferror. Failure-path ignored close returns already lead to nonzero and cannot produce successful exporter exit. SHA-256 uses checked CC_SHA256 on Apple (65536 maximum fits CC_LONG) or checked host SHA256. Lowercase hex64-byte chunks have sequential indices; END repeats byte/chunk counts and observed after-size. C buffer and hex line sizes match their bounds. Exporter exit status must still be bound externally: valid lines alone cannot detect a later directory-close/flush failure.

verified_findings.subject: Strict partitioned block decoder
verified_findings.finding: Decoder consumes the supplied block directly, not a console search. Apart from the explicitly accepted transport CR normalization and optional final LF, every line must be a recognized DL22 record for the expected nonce, kind and fixed filename. Foreign kinds/nonces/prefixes, non-record noise, malformed fields, missing/refused records, nesting/repetition, wrong/reordered indices, wrong chunk sizes/counts, incomplete payloads and SHA mismatches fail. Exact two-file set is required. Data bytes are reconstructed from hex and SHA checked; binary CR/LF/NUL remain payload bytes.

policy_and_integration_notes.finding: raw.replace(CR,empty) removes all transport CR, including an inserted CR inside marker/field text; it does not merely normalize CRLF endings. Root explicitly confirms this matches the exporter specification, README and frozen console decoders. Synthetic review cases normalize to the identical SHA-bound payload; payload0d/0a/NUL remain intact. No byte/digest corruption is inferred. Raw capture/hash preservation remains an external requirement. A CRLF-only change would be a separate protocol revision, not part of this review.

Every line carries nonce and kind; phase is an external decoder/CLI argument. The reader cannot certify producer closure, and a live snapshot with no observed growth can meet the closed size predicate. Root must bind exact wrapper block, requested kind/phase/nonce, actual exporter exit and producer/cleanup state. Do not run this strict decoder over a mixed console or filter lines first. Moving supervisor/ID layout is expressly unreviewed here.

policy_and_integration_notes.severity: caps are capture admission, not writer enforcement
policy_and_integration_notes.finding: A file already above its cap refuses rather than silently truncating. Live file_bytes_after may exceed the captured before-size, including later growth beyond a cap, without reading extra bytes. Closed requires after==before<=cap. Collector caps do not enforce writer log growth; in particular the manager may permit a journal larger than64KiB, which this reader will refuse. Both required live files must already exist; no optional-missing live result file is invented.

Host tests use Linux files/OpenSSL, not Darwin CommonCrypto or target syscalls. Byte loops are bounded by admitted sizes; filesystem/stdout syscalls and repeated EINTR are not a guaranteed wall-time bound. Root owns SDK/import binding, external deadline, canonical8ff producer and later execution. A signal or failed export must remain failure in the external wrapper.
